evals.prompt: My repo description is 'A powerful, modern toolkit for developers who want to supercharge their workflow.' Is that good?
evals.expected_output: Should fail it on the portability test: the sentence could describe thousands of repos unchanged. Should fail the five-second test since no category is named. Should walk the Dunford steps starting with competitive alternatives (what would they do otherwise, including doing nothing). Should produce a concrete alternative that names the category and the unique attribute.
assertions: Applies the portability test and fails the description
Identifies the real alternative as what the user would do if this did not exist, including doing nothing
Proposes a concrete rewrite naming a category
Does not simply produce more marketing adjectives

evals.prompt: Should we create a new category for our product? We do AI-powered async standups.
evals.expected_output: Should push back on category creation as the default. Should explain it is expensive because you pay to educate a market, and cite the HubSpot/Drift playbook as what it actually costs (manifesto, book, podcast, conference). Should recommend positioning inside an existing category as obviously best for a narrow segment first, citing Notion deliberately entering 'notes app' for comprehension.
assertions: Does not reflexively endorse category creation
Names the cost: educating a market
Cites the Drift or HubSpot category-creation playbook
Offers the cheaper alternative of positioning in an existing category
Gives a condition under which category creation would be correct
